items.prose: Break a stick of length 1 at two uniform points.
items.question: What is the chance every piece is longer than $\tfrac15$? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Set aside $\tfrac15$ for each piece, then split what is left.

byKey.one: That is the chance one named piece is longer than $\tfrac15$.
byKey.nosq: You found what is left, $\tfrac25$. Two cuts share it, so square it.

explain.text: Reserve $\tfrac15$ for each piece; two uniform cuts share the other $\tfrac25$. The chance scales as $(1 - 3a)^2 = 0.16$.

items.prose: Break a stick of length 1 at two uniform points $X$ and $Y$.
items.question: What is the expected length of the piece between the two breaks?

options.why: You took the mean of one break. The middle piece is $|X - Y|$, smaller on average.
That is the chance of a triangle, not a length.

feedback.correct: $E|X - Y| = \tfrac13$, the same as each of the three pieces.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The middle piece is $|X - Y|$.

explain.text: The middle piece is $|X - Y|$, with mean $\tfrac13$ from l18. By symmetry every piece averages $\tfrac13$, and the three add to 1.

items.prose: Seven points fall uniformly on a circle.
items.question: What is the chance they lie in one semicircle? Give four decimal places.

byKey.power-n: You used $2^7$. The start point is in its own half for certain.
byKey.one-start: That is one fixed start. Any of the seven can start it.

explain.text: Seven disjoint starts, each with chance $(\tfrac12)^6$: $\tfrac7{64}$.

items.prose: Points fall uniformly on a circle.
items.question: What is the smallest number of points for which the chance they lie in one semicircle is below 1%?

feedback.correct: $\tfrac{11}{1024} \approx 0.0107$ is still above 1%, and $\tfrac{12}{2048} \approx 0.0059$ is below: 12.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out $n/2^{n-1}$ for $n = 10, 11, 12$.

byKey.eleven: At 11 points the chance is $\tfrac{11}{1024} \approx 0.0107$, still just above 1%.
byKey.one-start: You dropped the factor $n$: $(\tfrac12)^7 < 0.01$. Every point can start the half.

explain.text: The chance halves with each point, less a little for the growing $n$. At 11 points it is 1.07%, at 12 it is 0.59%.

items.prose: Uniforms on $[0, 1]$ are added until the sum passes 1; $N$ is the number drawn.
items.question: What is $P(N = 4)$? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the difference of two tail chances.

explain.text: $N = 4$ means three draws are not enough but four are. So $\tfrac16 - \tfrac1{24} = \tfrac18$.

items.prose: Two people arrive at uniform times in one hour. Each waits 6 minutes.
items.question: What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use $w = 0.1$ in $1 - (1 - w)^2$.

byKey.lin: You added the waits, 12 of 60. The band is clipped at the corners.
byKey.one: That is one wait over the hour. Either may come first.

explain.text: The corners leave a $54 \times 54$ square of misses: $0.81$. So they meet with chance 0.19.

items.prose: A waits 5 minutes for B; B waits 25 minutes for A. Arrivals are uniform in one hour.
items.question: What is the chance they meet? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The two corners have legs 55 and 35.

byKey.avg: You averaged the waits to 15. The corners are $55^2/2$ and $35^2/2$, not two $45^2/2$.
byKey.sum: You added the waits, 30 of 60. The band is clipped at the corners.

explain.text: B coming more than 5 after A leaves a corner with legs 55. A coming more than 25 after B leaves one with legs 35. So $1 - \tfrac{1512.5 + 612.5}{3600} = \tfrac{59}{144}$.

items.prose: A needle of length 0.8 falls on lines 1 apart.
items.question: What is the chance it crosses a line? Give four decimal places.

explain.text: The chance is linear in the length: $0.8 \times \tfrac2{\pi} \approx 0.509$.

items.prose: Needles of length $\tfrac34$ fall on lines 1 apart. In 10,000 drops, 4,780 cross.
items.question: Estimate $\pi$ to four decimal places.

byKey.no-l: You used a unit needle. This one has $l = \tfrac34$.
byKey.no-both: You dropped both the 2 and the length.

explain.text: The share 0.478 estimates $\tfrac{1.5}{\pi}$, so $\pi \approx 1.5 / 0.478$. About 4,775 crossings were expected, so this run is close.

items.question: What is the expected range, largest minus smallest? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract the expected minimum from the expected maximum.

byKey.max: That is the expected maximum. Subtract the minimum, $\tfrac15$.

explain.text: The range is max minus min on every outcome, so $E = \tfrac45 - \tfrac15 = \tfrac35$. That is $\tfrac{n - 1}{n + 1}$ at $n = 4$.
